multi_patch_runtime_cancellation_partial.results: Internal runtime-oriented multi-patch orchestration recovers pending state, prepares a candidate, acquires the exclusive journal and publishes while consulting the live agent cancellation token directly. Cancellation after the first file and during the final commit check triggers rollback; cancellation before start creates no journal. Current-source real-file publication tests (16), full workspace library (204), recovery tests (12), patch tests (7), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy, fmt/diff passed. This seam is not registered or advertised as a tool; per-path durable approvals, hooks, crash-safe stage cleanup and broader operations remain open.

production_multi_publish_crash_evidence.results: Real child-process kills exercise the production workspace publisher: after first replacement, reopening restores original bytes; external changes instead remain intact with the intent pending. A separate kill after production staging and before an intent demonstrates two untracked staging files; the first-replacement recovery clears its journal while one staging file remains. The logs explicitly report these counts. The staging-only probe invokes the production adapter directly, not the full coordinator. Publication suite (20), recovery tests (12), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy, fmt/diff passed. Crash-safe cleanup is not implemented and remains a reason not to expose the tool.

multi_edit_staging_identity_partial.results: Recovery records now optionally carry a bounded, validated staging plan with an unpredictable-id format and per-file device/inode registrations. The locked journal can atomically persist a registration before staged bytes are written, requires the exact previous record, and rejects commit records that omit or change registered identity. Existing records without staging remain readable. Full workspace library (206), Rapid publication (20), recovery (12), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy and fmt/diff passed. This is foundation only: the production publisher still stages before intent, does not register identities and does not clean up crash leftovers. An unregistered existing stage must never be deleted solely by name; collision, inode-reuse and hostile namespace races require further handling.

journal_first_staging_partial.results: The Unix internal publisher now writes durable intent before staging; it generates a random id and records each exclusive-created empty stage device/inode before writing bytes. Recovery removes registered stages only when identity and intended-content prefix match; unregistered collisions, changed stages, external target conflicts and uncertain registrations retain the journal. Real-process tests verify restart cleanup after completed staging and after the first replacement; stage-collision, inode-replacement, partial-stage, final-registration and rollback tests passed. Full workspace library (209), publication (20), recovery (14), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy, fmt/diff passed. Crash after stage creation but before identity registration leaves an empty unregistered file and a pending journal requiring intervention; journal temp cleanup, hostile namespace races, full crash matrix, approval/hook integration and model exposure remain open.

journal_first_process_crash_boundaries_p.results: Test-only controlled pauses and real process kills exercise the production multi-file publisher at empty stage creation before registration, immediately after registration, during a partial stage write, after first replacement, during rollback restoration, during stage cleanup, and after committed intent before settlement. Registered and partial stages are cleaned; a committed transaction retains completed edits; interrupted rollback/cleanup finishes on restart; an unregistered empty mode-0600 file remains untouched with its intent pending; external changes remain conflicts. Current-source publication suite (24), recovery suite (14), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy, fmt/diff passed. This is not a complete crash matrix: each target index, intent and registration fsync uncertainty, journal temporary records, hostile filesystem races, non-Unix behavior, approvals and hooks remain open.

multi_file_per_path_approval_partial.results: An internal multi-file approval chain binds each per-file request to a random chain id, call id, arguments, full candidate bytes/modes/order and one exact path. The ledger sink retrieves only resolved approved matching requests, and the chain rechecks each stored scope, summary and diff. The internal runtime requests paths one at a time and publishes only after all necessary decisions; denies win over asks, candidate/call changes invalidate grants, and live path policy is rechecked during commit. A real-ledger test reopens between both approvals and the final publication, using an in-process workspace and manually invoked internal seam. Chain tests (3), ledger query (1), full publication suite (30), recovery (14), Rapid/workspace all-target clippy and fmt/diff passed. This is not exposed to a model or integrated with live suspension, ACP/TUI approvals, hooks, formatting, process-restart read authority or the final crash matrix. Bounded ledger history can refuse long sessions.

multi_file_tool_surface_partial.results: Unix workspace_multi_patch is model-facing when pre/post tool hooks, formatters and shadow diagnostics are absent. The runtime validates each path and policy, requests candidate-bound approvals per path, journals publication, reports committed changes and serializes batches containing multi-file and ordinary edits. Current-source publication tests (33), tool-surface tests (5), real-binary loopback fresh/conflict/unread scenarios, real ACP separate-approval/deny/stale scenarios, Rapid/workspace all-target clippy, fmt/diff passed. The full ACP CLI suite passed 26 on the immediately preceding source snapshot before final error-message and test-only changes. REF-016 remains open: hooks/formatters, create/delete support, non-Unix, unregistered empty-stage recovery, journal temp cleanup, hostile external races and final workspace/platform acceptance are not complete.

multi_file_create_delete_partial.results: Unix workspace_multi_patch now accepts exactly one ordered-patch, create or delete operation per path. Existing deletions require fresh visible read proofs, creations require absence and an existing parent and use mode 0600, and approval previews name action/path and creation mode. Current-source publication tests (37) include mixed operations and real process kills after creation and deletion; approval tests (3), real-binary fresh/unread/existing and patch regression scenarios (2 tests), real ACP approved/denied action-preview test, Rapid/workspace all-target clippy and fmt/diff passed. Hooks/formatters, non-Unix, automatic handling of an unregistered empty stage, hostile external filesystem races and final workspace/platform acceptance remain open.

multi_file_lsp_partial.results: Unix workspace_multi_patch is now available with language-server-only write steps. After a committed transaction it sends each surviving candidate image to the configured session language server, redacts and bounds combined notes, skips deleted paths, and reports diagnostics in the tool result. A real local Python LSP subprocess reported diagnostics for both committed files; the tool remains hidden and refuses direct calls when formatters are configured. Current-source publication tests (39), single-file LSP regression, ACP multi-file approval regression, Rapid/workspace all-target clippy and fmt/diff passed. Formatting, shadow diagnostics, pre/post hooks, non-Unix support and remaining recovery edge cases remain open.

headless_question_real_write_crash_parti.results: A real rapid questions recover process resumes a committed structured answer against a loopback OpenAI-compatible model, applies a workspace_write, and is killed while the next provider request is held. Reopening the ledger reports the claimed continuation uncertain, refuses another claim and the real CLI refuses another recover; the production tool effect remains. A scripted turn-runtime worker separately pauses after a real WorkspaceTools write. The complete approval-flow suite (13), Rapid all-target clippy, fmt and diff passed. This uses a loopback model and does not prove credentialed-provider behavior, every crash boundary, or all surfaces.
